goal: Pre-build implementation design for all KB capabilities and coordinated dashboard
source_policy: Reuse same-day audit evidence; refresh decision-relevant primary references; user requirements outrank examples; no superiority inferred from source descriptions.

briefs.type: local audited code and design packet
briefs.confidence: high for cited source behavior; unverified live state
briefs.goal: Preserve all capabilities while turning the audit into bounded implementation work.
claims: Production composition gaps exist despite passing component tests.
Existing governance, strict boundary decoders, broker confinement and provenance are useful foundations.
Whole-document hydration and distributed lifecycle ownership need simplification.
briefs.sequence: Contain known failure paths; prove an early isolated vertical; compare runtimes; integrate remaining capabilities; cut over only after parity and restore evidence.
briefs.takeaway: Use source-backed acceptance, not feature inventories, as the completion criterion.
briefs.writeup: KB's audit supports simplifying mutable runtime authority while preserving reviewed definitions, content-bound human grants and artifact provenance. The 706 selected passing cases are historical audit evidence, not this design turn's tests or live readiness.

briefs.accessibility: source accessible; refreshed queue-mode docs endpoint returned unsupported text/markdown
briefs.confidence: high for inspected worker code; moving branch unpinned
briefs.goal: Separate execution capacity and shutdown from dashboard presentation.
claims: Worker code sets queue execution mode, has explicit concurrency and shuts down active executions.
briefs.sequence: Configure worker capacity, run queue work, drain active executions on shutdown.
briefs.takeaway: Borrow a small worker lifecycle contract; adopting n8n wholesale is not necessary.
briefs.writeup: The inspected worker exposes a concrete capacity and shutdown boundary. KB should prove equivalent lifecycle behavior through its actual composition and broker, without importing n8n's entire infrastructure stack.

briefs.confidence: high for documented semantics; suitability unmeasured
briefs.goal: Challenge the cost of custom recovery machinery.
claims: Workflow event history supports replay and deterministic reconstruction.
briefs.sequence: Record workflow progress; replay after interruption; separate deterministic orchestration from external activities.
briefs.takeaway: Run an identical-workflow candidate comparison before choosing the runtime.
briefs.writeup: Temporal is a genuine candidate, not just inspiration to recreate its features. Compare recovery correctness, retained custom code, processes, upgrade burden and operator effort. No performance or maintenance advantage is assumed in advance.

briefs.accessibility: accessible and refreshed; durable-execution URL redirects here
briefs.goal: Make agent continuation and memory scopes explicit.
claims: Checkpointers hold thread-scoped state; stores hold cross-thread data.
In-memory checkpoints do not survive process restart.
briefs.sequence: Persist thread checkpoints and separate longer-lived knowledge; define retention and restart behavior.
briefs.takeaway: Borrow durable waits/checkpoint boundaries, not another platform authority.
briefs.writeup: Graph checkpointing can help an individual agent workflow. It does not replace platform authorization, worker leases, signed deployment or canonical result publication.

briefs.goal: Clarify worker capability, capacity and availability in the dashboard.
claims: Work pools separate orchestration from execution infrastructure and expose inherited configuration and limits.
Only some pool types require a separately run worker.
briefs.sequence: Bind deployment to a pool; enforce its capacity and infrastructure contract; report worker/queue availability.
briefs.takeaway: Use explicit capability and capacity states; do not equate authentication or a running daemon with worker readiness.
briefs.writeup: KB can adapt the pool boundary into its worker adapters. The goal is an operator-visible and testable contract, not adoption of Prefect's entire deployment system.

briefs.type: primary repository documentation; cached prior source comparison
briefs.confidence: high for kit category; integration advantage unmeasured
briefs.goal: Keep agent roles, skills and handoffs portable and scoped.
claims: ECC packages skills, memory, security and harness configuration across coding-agent runtimes.
briefs.sequence: Load relevant instructions and roles; run bounded work; retain reviewed memory and handoff evidence.
briefs.takeaway: Reuse scoped skills and review practices while keeping durable orchestration elsewhere.
briefs.writeup: ECC is an agent harness/configuration kit, not a substitute for KB's scheduler or durable runtime. KB already imports related review and session practices; duplication or wholesale installation is unnecessary.
